speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon
text: asked	the Minister for Health whether there are ways to help families who are unable to qualify for additional Government subsidies to pay for outpatient medical fees that may cost thousands of dollars even after basic Government subsidies, such as that for MRIs, CT scans, and blood tests.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: These include initiatives to focus on health promotion and disease prevention, as well as efforts to improve productivity and develop our primary care and intermediate and long-term care facilities in the community.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: Day surgery is also covered by MediShield Life and MediSave.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: MOH will regularly review the scope of MediShield Life's coverage, but the focus should remain on protecting Singaporeans against large hospital bills.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: It is important to bear in mind that expansions in MediShield Life coverage will lead to higher premiums for all policyholders.

speaker: The Minister of State for Health (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Minister for Health)
text: And with an ageing population, we need to carefully consider the trade-offs to ensure that the schemes remain affordable and sustainable.

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: If this happens, does it lead to a misallocation of beds?

speaker: Mr Ong Teng Koon (Marsiling-Yew Tee)
text: And is it something that the Ministry is looking at and thinking of ways to solve the problem?

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: As explained in my answer, right-siting is an important priority for our healthcare system, because we do want to make sure that patients receive appropriate care at the appropriate location that is most suitable for their medical condition.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: So, if the patient requires inpatient services, then he or she rightly should be hospitalised.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: But if the patient does not require that, then outpatient treatment would be more appropriate.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: We do need to look at our financing scheme – how the incentives are being set to ensure that we are able to support right-siting, which is a key part of ensuring a more sustainable healthcare system.

speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
text: That is something that we have at the hospitals and polyclinics, whether it is for inpatient or for outpatient treatment.
